support_summary: D1: single author-chosen topic from the author's own research area (yohimbine pharmacokinetics/CYP2D6) probed in one sequential conversation, with follow-up prompts written after seeing the answers (Par1-Par13), in a narrow sparse area where fabrication is more likely; D2: prompts printed verbatim and model given as free ChatGPT Version 1.2024.170 on a Mac, which is GPT-4o, but no generation date is stated; D3: no generation settings, outputs-per-prompt or retry rule reported anywhere in the letter; D4: the fabrication call rests on the supplied PubMed IDs/links, which exist but point to different authors, topics and journals (Par40), with no explicit verification method and no second source stated before references were called nonexistent; D5: the sole author both ran the conversation and verified the references, with no separation of roles stated; D6: single unblinded verifier, no duplicate verification and no agreement figure; D7: no partial-match rule stated in advance, but all 5 references are printed in full with components described apart (authors real, journals real target journals, titles nonexistent, PubMed IDs mismatched, Par40); D8: the single conversation and all 5 references it produced are reported in full, with no arm or topic dropped.

D1: 10 author-prepared audiology questions with no sampling frame, listed in full in Table 1 and deliberately balanced as basic (1-3), intermediate (4-6) and specialised (7-10) (Methods); D2: questions printed verbatim in Table 1 and run date stated (presented 28.08.2023) on standard publicly available versions, but exact versions are incomplete - ChatGPT version 3.5, Bing Chat based on GPT-4 with modifications, Bard PaLM 2 marked experimental with no release string; D3: no temperature or equivalent settings and no retry rule reported, though differing live-internet access across arms is described (ChatGPT none, Bing Chat and Bard live) and one response per question per chatbot was evaluated, including Bard's failure to answer question 3; D4: no bibliographic verification source is named for references - provision of sources was only counted (Table 2, ChatGPT 0/10, Bing Chat 8/10, Bard 2/10) and responses rated for correctness by expert impression, with no existence or field-level check of the supplied sources against PubMed, Crossref or any other source; D5: the two authors prepared and posed the questions and also evaluated the responses, with no separation between generation and verification stated and no vendor role reported; D6: both experts went over all responses twice and agreed on the scores (Methods), but verification was not independent or blinded to chatbot identity and no agreement figure is reported; D7: no reference-level rule for partial matches and no partial-match counts for references - only an answer-level distinction that small mistakes were rated as inaccuracies when imprecise although not misleading (Methods); D8: all 3 chatbots and all 10 questions named in Methods are reported with counts in Table 2, with full responses in Supplementary Files 1-3 and Bard's non-response to question 3 reported rather than dropped.
